references.text: Isaiah 43:1 is a direct parallel where God promises to deliver His people from captivity, setting the stage for the theme of true liberation that Jesus presents in John 8:36.

Isaiah 61:1 proclaims that the Messiah will come to preach freedom to the captives, a theme Jesus Himself cited as fulfilled in Luke, and which lies at the heart of the promise to become truly free in John 8:36.

Galatians 5:1 urges believers to stand firm in the freedom Christ has given them and warns against being entangled again under a yoke, reflecting Jesus' warning and promise of true freedom in John 8:36.
Romans 8:2 introduces the law of the Spirit who gives life as setting one free from the law of sin and death, a theological elaboration of the spiritual liberation that Jesus promises in John 8:36.
Galatians 4:31 concludes that we are not children of the slave woman but of the free woman, a direct theological link to the contrast between slavery to sin and freedom in Christ found in John 8:36.
